office_does: The assessor values every taxable property in Franklin County at market value, calculates levy rates from the budgets taxing districts set, and runs property tax exemptions.
race_blurb: Two Republicans: incumbent John A. Rosenau, assessor since 2021, against state-certified appraiser Chris Hollingsworth, who led the August primary with 54.1% to Rosenau's 44.7%. Both promise fair, consistent assessments; the race turns on record versus a practitioner's critique of the office.

candidates.summary: State-certified residential appraiser with about 20 years in private practice and a Republican precinct committee officer, challenging the incumbent assessor.
highlights: Appraiser licensed since 2004 who owns a practice covering four counties [S1][S2]
Says he ran after helping residents at Board of Equalization hearings and promises to 'restore confidence' in the office [S1]
Promises appraisal training, strict professional standards and open communication with owners [S1]
Endorsed by the Tri-Cities Association of Realtors; Realtors' PAC gave $1,200 [S1][S4]

experience.basis: Challenger who has never held county office, running on outside professional appraisal experience to change how the office works.

spending.basis: Platform is oversight, professional standards and accuracy in an office he says needs restored confidence, not new programs.

candidates.summary: Franklin County Assessor since 2021, a former bank regional manager and police chief who chairs a regional assessors' group and sits on the state assessors' executive board.
highlights: Cites stronger training, consistent valuations and clear standards in the office [S1]
Has pushed at the state assessors' association for tax relief through exemptions for seniors, people with disabilities, farmers and small businesses [S1]
Endorsed by more than 30 county assessors and the office's AFSCME appraisers' local [S1]

experience.basis: Incumbent seeking a further term on his record in office, with statewide association roles and peer endorsements.

taxes.basis: Advocates property tax relief through broader exemptions; otherwise stresses that the assessor does not set tax levels.
